summary.text: The captured page, given as a student data story about Seattle library visits, is laid out as a stock product landing page: a launch-style hero with a 'Get started' button, a strip of unitless performance figures, three icon cards, an FAQ, a single chart, and a closing call to action. Across that skeleton the evidence shows a recurring purple-to-blue glow-on-dark palette, numbered eyebrow labels on every section, one sparkle badge on unrelated cards, and broad 'unlock / transform / seamless' copy that never names Seattle, the data, the period, or a finding. The one chart has no axes, labels, values, or source, and its caption is two words. These are features that can make the page read as template scaffolding with little data story inside it; they say nothing about who or what made the site, and each has benign explanations such as pitch framing chosen for class, an unrevised starter template, or work in progress. Limits: no interactions were recorded, so the buttons and FAQ disclosures are untested rather than broken; FAQ answers, alt text, and hidden content were not captured; only one route was captured, and the mobile screenshots cover the upper part of the page.
